_comment: What Foreman does, in the order it happens to a real enquiry. Written to be SCANNED, not read: a tradesperson is looking at this on a phone, standing up, between jobs. Short title, one line, three short proof points. If a card needs a paragraph, the card is wrong. `art` picks an icon from lib/illustrations.mjs — icons must mean what the card says.
flowNote: Four things, in that order, every time an enquiry comes in.
problemHeading: You don't lose jobs on price. You lose them on silence.
problemLede: A customer rings three firms at lunchtime. One picks up. That one usually gets the work — and it's rarely the cheapest. The rest leaks out of quotes nobody chased.

problems.label: calls to a working trade go unanswered
problems.note: You're under a floor, up a ladder, or driving.

problems.label: the job you lose by not calling back
problems.note: One a month is a salary a year.

_statsComment: Industry-shaped framing, not measured claims about Foreman. Source them or soften them to 'most' and 'often' before launch — an unsourced percentage is the first thing a sceptical buyer challenges.
doesLede: Six jobs. Each one is somewhere work currently leaks out.

capabilities.title: Answers in under a minute
capabilities.body: Day, night, Sunday. A missed call becomes a text before they've dialled the next firm.
detail: Sounds like you, not a robot

capabilities.title: Asks what you'd have asked
capabilities.body: Boiler make and age. Which rooms, what floor, parking. You know if it's worth the drive before you drive.

capabilities.title: Quotes from your price book
capabilities.body: Your rates, your margins, your letterhead. Out today instead of Sunday night.

capabilities.title: Chases till you get an answer
capabilities.body: This is where the money is. Three polite nudges, stopping the second they reply.
detail: Asks why, if it's a no

capabilities.title: Books the survey
capabilities.body: Offers slots you've actually got free, then reminds them the day before.

capabilities.title: Shows you what's working
capabilities.body: In, quoted, won — and what each source is really worth. Most trades are paying for one that's never produced a job.

approvalHeading: It won't talk to your customers behind your back
approvalBody: Every message comes to you first. You read it, tap approve, it sends. Leave that on forever if you like — most people switch it off for the routine stuff after a fortnight and keep it on for the big quotes. It's your name on the van.
integrationsBody: Foreman is a sales desk, not another job system. Tradify, Jobber, ServiceM8, or a diary and a notebook — it works alongside, not instead.
_integrationsComment: Do not list named integrations as available until they are built and tested. Naming one you have not integrated with is the quickest way to lose a demo.
